stimulus.source_note: John Brown, address to the Virginia court, November 2, 1859, before sentencing for the Harpers Ferry raid. Public domain. Wording verified against the Gilder Lehrman transcript (Address of John Brown to the Virginia Court, GLC05508.051) and the Dickinson House Divided text. The two passages appear in this order in the address; omissions are marked.
stimulus.text: I never did intend murder, or treason, or the destruction of property, or to excite or incite slaves to rebellion, or to make insurrection. . . . I believe that to have interfered as I have done . . . in behalf of His despised poor, was not wrong, but right.

rationales.A: “I deny everything but what I have all along admitted, of a design on my part to free slaves.”
rationales.B: Brown denies intending murder; he says his design was to free slaves, not to kill slaveholders.
rationales.C: Brown wanted the arsenal’s rifles to arm enslaved people, not land for himself.
rationales.D: Brown’s quarrel was with slavery, not with Virginia as a state.
rationales.general:
1. Hear Brown deny: no murder, no treason, no destruction of property, no insurrection.
2. Hear him admit: one design only, to free slaves.
3. See his plan: seize the arsenal’s rifles and put them in enslaved people’s hands.
4. See the verdict: the court sentenced Brown to hang, and he died on December 2, 1859.
Remember: a defendant facing death chooses his words with care; believe the design he admits.
